"My name is David van der Veer, a first-year Technical Computer Science student at Avans University of Applied Sciences in Breda.
During my time in the program, I have participated in several projects, which I will showcase in this app with photos and descriptions. In my free time, I enjoy working on personal projects. My current personal project is still in progress, which is why it is not included in this app yet.
As a motivated second-year Technical Computer Science student at Avans University of Applied Sciences in Breda, I am currently looking for a part-time job that I can do alongside my studies, preferably about two days a week. In the past, I worked at a metalworking company, where I discovered that while I enjoy working with technology, I also want to make more use of and further develop my social skills.
I enjoy learning and improving new skills, and I consider myself a social and communicative person. I am fluent in both Dutch and English and can make myself understood in German to some extent. I take initiative when I feel it’s appropriate and can quickly get a good overview of what needs to be done. I can think critically when solving problems if expected, but I am also perfectly capable of following instructions and completing tasks efficiently."

string-array.name: short_description_projects
string-array.item: This is the first project I did during my studies. It was a simple project where a UI had to be combined with basic calculations related to the weather.
AGV was the first project where we were taught to work with hardware. During this project, the focus was on getting actuators, such as motors, to work together with sensors.
In this project, we worked with 2D graphics for the first time. The goal was to create an app where a train station schedule could be planned and then actually simulated in another part of the app.
The idea behind the project in module 1.4 was to design and develop a system that combined custom-built hardware with an Android app.
A mini project where the goal was to create an app that could function as a résumé (CV).
For this project, we had to use an ergometer to read data and set up a network system involving both patients and doctors in order to simulate a hospital application.
Period 2.2 was focused on Mobile Systems. During this time, we used the cross-platform framework MAUI to create an app that provided a tour through the city of Breda.
During this period, we worked with embedded systems for the first time. The goal was to create a smart speaker that could detect and play audio. This was also our first real experience using Scrum.

I personally found the Augmented Reality project very interesting. We had to use the webcam to create interaction with the user through an app. For this, we designed a game similar to the once-popular game Temple Run.

string-array.name: detailed_description_projects
string-array.item: In period 1 of my first year as a Technical Informatics student, I worked on creating a set of algorithms that can process weather data from a weather station. I did this together with a group of fellow first-year students. Personally, my tasks in this project included controlling the given GUI board, writing an algorithm that finds the median for each data measurement over a period, and converting the raw data (American measurements without decimals) into readable data (European values with decimals in the correct place).

In period 2 of my first year, our project assignment was to build an automated guided vehicle. We received the specifications during the first weeks of the project from the "client." For us, this meant creating a robot that could deliver feed to goats at a petting zoo. Personally, during this project, I spent a lot of time working on the code structure and making the somewhat messy code more robust. Through this, I learned how the entire robot worked and what makes a piece of code reliable.

The project I worked on together with my fellow students in period 3 of my first year was a GUI that could be used to plan a train schedule for a station and visualize it through a simulation. In this project, I mainly worked on the C(reate).R(ead).U(pdate).D(elete) functions of the planner. I also created a visual clock in the simulation to improve the user experience, and I focused on adding a slider that allows the simulation time to be sped up or slowed down.

In period 4 of my first year, my team and I were assigned to create a user experience for the fictional park "de Essteling." During this period, I acted as project leader and further developed myself in this role, which was my main goal for the period. Besides my role, I worked on designing the final product, which we eventually called the Magic Arcade, and I contributed significantly to it. Furthermore, I actually realized almost all the designs, including wiring diagrams, controller designs, and soldering all the components together.

This is a standalone project, separate from all the so-called "professional tasks" of my first year. The goal of this assignment was to develop an application that can function as a résumé (CV). For this, I applied the theory I learned in user experience design and thoroughly studied how to use Android Studio. Personally, I am very proud of my achievement, as I was nervous to start this app at first due to having spent little time on the professional task (the Magic Arcade). However, I think this app turned out well. I made sure everything is clearly readable and works regardless of whether it is used on a new or old device (down to Android 10 at least), and whether the device is small or large.
